analysis:
Examined all supplied test source, patches and metadata against the canonical index and supplied T-041 detail. No concrete security regression is established by these test-only changes; assertions are not proof of production enforcement.
GLM5ToolFailureTests.swift head 33–48 replaces forced-tool refusal expectations with a native, nonstreaming parser and structured post-validation. Lines 52–91 exercise atomic rejection of malformed/truncated/oversized output without exposing content or earlier calls. Integration must verify scheduler/parser validation and buffering bounds for the new forced-tool path (A-001, T-007, TB-007).
GLM5NextMediaRoutingTests.swift head 237–265 asserts JSON and forced-tool media requests are rejected before preparation/submission. Lines 293–340 exercise local, hash-checked QuickTime/MP4 fixtures through real ingest/processor normalization, but substitute a synthetic image submission at line 324; this does not establish actual video-engine execution, resource admission or cancellation. Review accompanying ingest changes for decode/frame/byte limits, temporary plaintext handling and cancellation (TB-007, T-050, T-010). Existing reservation tests remain intact. Fixture paths are fixed test inputs, not caller-controlled network fetches.
GLM5NextProviderLoopTests.swift patch head 194–220 adds expectations that redundant WeightHasher reads disappear while live and persisted hashes equal the manifest aggregate. Integration must verify the managed loader hashes the exact consumed bytes, binds persisted file identities without a substitution race, and publishes only verified digests (A-004, T-012, T-027; T-041 cache weightHash binding). The supplied tests use unchanged files and cannot establish those contracts. Prefix storage is explicitly disabled in the host fixture; retirement/unwind tests are unchanged. No supplied changes touch attestation grants, encryption, credentials, billing or privileged-helper authority. Production implementations and the remaining PR are outside this batch, leaving these material cross-file questions for integration.
